fields.columns: | columns event.time, event.type, site.name, agent.uuid, src.process.storyline.id, src.process.user, src.process.uid, src.process.cmdline, src.ip.address, src.port.number, dst.ip.address, dst.port.number, src.process.parent.cmdline, tgt.process.cmdline
fields.description:
Detects the creation of a child "explorer.exe" process from a shell like process such as "cmd.exe" or "powershell.exe".
Attackers can use "explorer.exe" for evading defense mechanisms by proxying the execution through the latter.
While this is often a legitimate action, this rule can be use to hunt for anomalies.
Muddy Waters threat actor was seeing using this technique.
fields.name: Potential Proxy Execution Via Explorer.EXE From Shell Process
fields.notes:
- To move around freely without attracting too much attention, attackers often use reliable software (one of the favorites is psexec) that looks normal in an enterprise environment.
- Use the following aggregate to easily group by endpoint: `| group array_agg_distinct(dst.ip.address) by endpoint.name, src.process.cmdline`
fields.query: event.type="Process Creation" and (endpoint.os="windows" and ((src.process.image.path contains "\cmd.exe" or src.process.image.path contains "\powershell.exe" or src.process.image.path contains "\pwsh.exe") and tgt.process.image.path contains "\explorer.exe" and tgt.process.cmdline contains "explorer.exe"))
